items.title: Quantization of charge (q = Ne) and electrostatics

source_refs.note: Opening of Chapter 9 before topic 9.1 (PDF 192-193, printed 189-190). The learning objectives are not reproduced.

blocks.text: We know that the magnitude of the charge on an electron is equal to that of a proton. The charge on a proton is e+ and that on an electron is e-. Its value is e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, where C (coulomb) is the SI unit of charge. This charge e is the smallest amount of free charge that has been discovered.

Charges of larger magnitude are built up on an object by adding or removing electrons. Since e is the minimum amount of charge that any particle may contain, any amount of charge q is an integer multiple of e:

blocks.title: Quantization of charge
blocks.text: q = Ne, where N is an integer. Charge comes only in whole-number multiples of the electronic charge e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C.

blocks.title: Electrostatics
blocks.text: Electrostatics is the study of phenomena and properties of electric charges at rest. When charges are in motion, we call it an electric current.

Charles de Coulomb (1736-1806): Coulomb's major contribution to science was in the field of electrostatics and magnetism. During his lifetime he also investigated the strengths of materials and determined the forces that affect beams, thereby contributing to the field of structural mechanics. In the field of ergonomics, his research provided a fundamental understanding of the ways in which people and animals can best do work.

blocks.prompt: Is a charge of 2.5 x 10^-19 C or of 3.2 x 10^-19 C possible on a particle (MCQ 9.2)? How much charge can a battery rated at 100 A h supply (short question 9.3)?
blocks.explanation: Charge must be a whole-number multiple of e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C. 3.2 x 10^-19 C = 2e is possible (option b); 2.5 x 10^-19 C would be 1.56e, not a whole number, so it is not possible. A 100 A h battery can deliver 100 A for one hour: Q = It = 100 A x 3600 s = 3.6 x 10^5 C.

items: e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C is the smallest free charge; objects are charged by adding or removing electrons; q = Ne with N an integer (quantization of charge).
Electrostatics: charges at rest; charges in motion form an electric current.
